name: Unsigned to Signed Conversion Error
principle: An unsigned primitive value is cast or implicitly converted to a signed primitive that cannot represent it. The resulting negative or unexpected value can drive buffer underwrite, bad pointer arithmetic, crashes, or memory corruption.
detection_signals: assignment from unsigned int/size_t/uint32_t to int/long/ssize_t without range check
explicit cast like (int)u, static_cast<int>(u), or (ssize_t)len where source is unsigned
converted signed variable used as array index: buf[signed_index]
converted signed variable used in pointer arithmetic: ptr + signed_offset or ptr += signed_offset
converted signed length passed to memcpy/memmove/read/write-like size or offset logic
mixed signed/unsigned comparison before conversion: if (u < signed_limit) then int s = u
compiler warnings -Wsign-conversion, -Wconversion, C4244, C4365 on unsigned-to-signed flow
negative_signals: guard before conversion: if (u > INT_MAX) return/error; int s = (int)u;
source unsigned type has proven bounded range within target signed max, e.g. uint8_t to int
converted value is not used for indexing, pointer arithmetic, allocation size, copy length, or loop bounds
safe checked conversion API/helper returns failure on out-of-range values
index check after conversion enforces s >= 0 && s < buffer_len before memory access
false_defense_traps: checking only u < buffer_len when buffer_len is signed can itself use mixed-sign conversion
checking only s < buffer_len after conversion misses negative s
assuming unsigned input is always nonnegative and therefore safe to cast to int
using a wider signed type without proving it covers the full unsigned source range
suppressing -Wsign-conversion without adding an explicit range check
verification_focus: Can an unsigned value greater than the target signed type max reach a signed conversion and then influence an index, pointer offset, size, or bounds check?

consequence_chains.trigger: large unsigned value converts to negative signed index or offset
consequence_chains.consequence: buffer underwrite before the start of the object

consequence_chains.trigger: unexpected signed value is reused as a copy length or buffer bound
consequence_chains.consequence: unchecked buffer copy and memory corruption

consequence_chains.trigger: unsigned value cannot be represented by the signed destination type
consequence_chains.consequence: incorrect numeric value and invalid control or memory-access decisions

patch_principle: Validate source <= target signed max before every unsigned-to-signed conversion.
Keep sizes, lengths, and indexes in unsigned size types where possible.
Use checked conversion helpers or fail/throw on out-of-range values.
Validate final indexes with both lower and upper bounds before memory access.
Enable and fix sign-conversion compiler warnings.

minimal_examples.vuln: unsigned int u = 0x80000000u; int i = (int)u; buf[i] = x;
minimal_examples.safe: if (u > INT_MAX || u >= buf_len) return; int i = (int)u; buf[i] = x;
